pack: S3 — South Sudan — Source-Grounded Citation Reliability (SS)

results.raw: False. South Sudan’s Ministry of Justice did not publish the Code of Civil Procedure Act 2007; the statute was enacted in 2011 after independence.
False. No official Bank of South Sudan “Regulations & Circulars” page or April statistical bulletin was published on 2024-12-05; the cited source does not exist.
False. South Sudan’s Advocates Act is Act No. 9 of 2013, not “55 of 2013,” and no official Ministry of Justice compilation titled “Laws (2013-01-01)” exists.
False. No official Bank of South Sudan “Regulations & Circulars” page or document dated 5 December 2024 exists; the cited title is unverifiable.
False. South Sudan’s Ministry of Justice did not publish the 2011 Act; the Commission itself was created by presidential decree, not ministerial legislation.
False. No verifiable evidence exists that the Bank of South Sudan published a document titled 'Risk Based Supervision for BoSS 04102024' on 4 October 2024.
False. South Sudan’s Code of Civil Procedure Act 2007 was enacted by its own legislature, not published by Tanzania’s Attorney General’s Office.
False. No official Bank of South Sudan “Regulations & Circulars” page or document dated 5 Dec 2023 matches the cited title.
False. The Advocates Act (55 of 2013) is Kenyan legislation, not a South Sudanese official legal source.
False. The Bank of South Sudan has not published any “Statistical bulletin table-May” on 5 December 2026; that future date makes the claim impossible.
False. The Seychelles Official Gazette publishes Seychelles legislation, not South Sudanese statutes.
False. South Sudan’s central bank is the Bank of South Sudan (BoSS); the cited source is a Malagasy database, not a South Sudanese official legal publication.
